name: Can I keep the window inside my primary shower without causing water damage?

mainEntity.name: Can I keep the window inside my primary shower without causing water damage?

acceptedAnswer.text: A window can remain in a shower area only when privacy, water exposure, ventilation, and waterproof detailing are addressed together. The existing window may need moisture-resistant materials, revised trim, a suitable sill, privacy glazing, or a different layout depending on its condition. Context: moving the shower may be simpler than forcing a vulnerable window into a wet zone, but that decision requires an actual room assessment. Key factors: window material, sill slope, exterior exposure, privacy, operability, and the shower spray pattern. Practical guidance: identify whether the window has swelling, peeling, condensation, or staining before demolition. Ask how the new waterproofing will connect around the opening. Elite Remodeling & Design can compare retaining, modifying, or relocating the wet-area layout during design.
acceptedAnswer.description: Possibly, but the window, sill, trim, privacy, and waterproof transitions must suit a wet area. Inspect for swelling and staining, then compare keeping the shower there with relocating it. The correct choice depends on the opening’s condition and the proposed waterproofing details.
